messages:
Maya D: dropped a compact-regression mock for prompt-set diffs: https://figma.com/file/compact-reg-diffs. main goals: scannability and keeping Approve prominent in dense lists. feedback? :mag:
Ethan B: quick pass  looks cleaner. flag: when rows compress we currently hide labels and rely on icons — we need clear aria-labels and distinct focus styles.
Rae S: agree. also think about keyboard shortcuts colliding with global shortcuts. if we have a keyboard 'A' to approve, it must only work when a row is focused. avoid global binding.
Maya D: plan: keep approve visible as primary CTA; other actions go into overflow. at widths <480px label becomes icon-only but button keeps aria-label="Approve result". shortcut handling: scoped to focused row only.
Ethan B: SR behavior: add a polite aria-live announce on action: "Result 3 approved". If multiple quick approves happen, debounce announcements to avoid spam.
Rae S: add acceptance criteria: 1) icon-only CTA has aria-label; 2) Tab order predictable (title -> CTA -> overflow); 3) keyboard shortcut scope enforced; 4) polite live region for approvals with 300ms debounce; 5) tooltip not relied on for SR users.
a11y-bot: Checklist updated: compact-regression -> icon-aria-labels, scoped-shortcuts, tab-order, polite-live-debounce, tooltip-not-only-label. See /docs/accessibility/compact-regression.md :white_check_mark:
Maya D: thanks! I'll update the mock and open a small PR with aria-labels + scoped shortcut handling. follow-ups: @Ethan B add keyboard tests; @Rae S run SR passes. target: behind flag next sprint. :rocket:
